pairs.why: B's clock rim and face are slightly softer and less lacquered than A's heavily glossy bevelled orange rim, closer to the real clock's moderate sheen.
B's lamp is matte navy with a soft sheen and little hard chrome, whereas A's bright chrome truss reads as shiny plastic and metal unlike the real cards' smooth satin finish.
Both domes are matte white regolith and glassy blue with near-identical finish and texture, so surface gives no reason to choose.
B's body is a smooth satin matte blue with soft highlights like the real calculator, while A's keys and body have glossier hard highlights and a chrome-like screen bezel.
A's door wood and plaster are a bit smoother and quieter, whereas B has more visible grain lines and rougher plaster.
A's brushed-metal head has soft satin gradients like the real cards, while B has more contrasty glints and busier rivet and pin hardware.
A's hat has a more matte white cloth and quiet floor grain like the real card, while B's floor and wall grain is busier.
A's trunk is smoother with fewer decorative marks, close to the real cards' smooth trunk with a few chunky cuts, while B's glossy trunk and leaves are slightly more lacquered.
